evidence_against: Short-horizon evidence is mixed: over the latest 4-hour window BTC returned -0.45% while ETH returned +0.56%; spot taker quote imbalance was positive for both assets, especially ETH, in the brief captured sample.
CFGI scores improved versus the prior capture (BTC 20.5 to 28, ETH 18.5 to 31, market 27.5 to 33), although all remain classified Fear.
The latest settled ETF session reported +137.3 BTC and -21.4 ETH, not uniformly negative flows; it is one session and does not establish broader transmission.

Historical protection calibration is low-confidence and descriptive: pullback risk was often marked building or elevated while distribution risk remained unknown. Outcomes and exit-reference opportunity costs varied by asset and horizon; overlapping freezes are not independent events.
evidence_for: The 24-hour and 72-hour API windows show declines in both assets: BTC -2.92% and -2.60%, ETH -3.25% and -2.87%, respectively. The 12-hour returns are smaller but still negative.

Direct ETH/BTC hourly closes were below 0.0300 for all 168 observed hours; the latest close was 0.0289. This is persistent relative weakness, not evidence by itself of a market-wide regime or distribution.

Latest proxy breadth is weak: 21 advancers and 78 decliners in the point-in-time filtered top-100 universe, with the prior capture showing 25 advancers and 74 decliners. Canonical breadth remains unconfirmed.

The separate rich-breadth proxy showed 23 advancers and 76 decliners at its earlier 07:16 UTC observation. It is proxy-only evidence and is not directly interchangeable with the later capture’s different membership and timestamp.

Fear classifications persist despite the modest CFGI improvement. The 30-, 90- and 365-day rotation scores are 27, 39 and 43 in the BlockchainCenter shadow series; the separate CMC published 90-day score is 45. Neither source indicates confirmed broad altcoin leadership.

The 24-hour net aggressive quote-flow sums were negative for BTC and ETH; the 72-hour sums were positive. This horizon disagreement cautions against treating one flow interval as persistent direction.
BTC dominance is available at 60.0469 for 2026-10-28 under the direct CMC convention. It is research context, not the TradingView top-125 convention.

This is more consistent with weak/fragile conditions and a possible retest than with a confirmed breakdown; short-horizon rebound evidence prevents a stronger directional conclusion. uncertainties: The API sequence is cross-horizon rather than fully uniform: 24- and 72-hour returns are negative, 12-hour moves are smaller, and the latest four-hour BTC/ETH returns diverge. The one-hour window has only one sample and a zero-hour actual span, so it does not support a meaningful directional inference.

News has no verified context item in the supplied record, but degraded ownership and an unverified discovery mean the absence of verified news cannot be interpreted as no event.
